newsitem.title: UK: WH Smith hits 20-mth low on ceo's departure.
newsitem.headline: WH Smith hits 20-mth low on ceo's departure.

text.p: Shares in WH Smith Plc dropped to their lowest level in 20 months on Tuesday amid negative press and analyst comment on Monday's departure of chief executive Bill Cockburn.
The stock was down 7p at 369-1/2 by 1003 GMT in volume of 767,480 shares, after falling as low as 357p -- its lowest since October 1995.
Analysts at BZW said they continued to rate the stock a "hold," arguing that the group's stores would find it difficult to maintain profits at a time of flat sales, marker sources said.
Comment in the Lex column of the Financial Times argued that WH Smith shares looked cheap at a 20 percent discount to the rest of the UK equity market but they were "likely to stay that way."
Lex said any hopes for a bid were likely to be disappointed and that shareholders would probably have to rely on the company's own efforts to boost the shares. "They will need to be patient."
